svg.title: Figure 3-2. Software architecture of the panda firmware and its host interface (WP-W-03 §3.2)
svg.desc: On the left, the QM host stack on the SoC (host.pandad) exchanges SPI4 transfers with the panda STM32H7, which runs the ASIL C safety envelope in one address space without MPU. U-PND-SPI passes control requests to U-PND-COMMS comms_control_handler: 0xdc goes to U-PND-MAIN set_safety_mode and then U-SAF-CORE set_safety_hooks, 0xf3 updates the heartbeat variables, 0xc5 drives the U-PND-HARN relay under the reference lock. CAN writes go through comms_can_write and can_send in U-PND-FDCAN to safety_tx_hook (U-SAF-CORE, U-SAF-TOY, U-SAF-LAT/LONG); accepted frames go to can_queues, process_can with XOR check and the FDCAN1/3 TX FIFO onto bus 0, rejected frames to rx_q. Frames received on bus 0 and bus 2 enter can_rx, which calls safety_fwd_hook (forwarded with can_send skipping the hook to the other bus) and safety_rx_hook (U-SAF-TOY rx, controls_allowed) and pushes them to rx_q, read by comms_can_read and sent over SPI to the SoC. Periodic contexts: TIM4 safety task at 100 Hz, TIM12 tick at 8 Hz with a 1 Hz branch, TIM6 at 1 Hz, and the main loop. Interfaces SI-01 to SI-10 of §3.3 are tagged.
svg.text: Figure 3-2 · Software architecture of the panda firmware
Units U-xxx (§3.1) and interfaces SI-xx (§3.3) · QM host stack on the SoC, ASIL C safety envelope on the panda STM32H7
one address space, no MPU · envelope code runs in interrupt context
